$comment: The wire-contract drift task U0.1 deliberately left behind, and the exact
set of test files it left failing. Read scripts/known-drift-gate.mjs for
how this file is used; read it before adding an entry.
Task U0.1 (2026-08-31, commit 6bf58f0) re-sourced wui/contract/ from
published Core v0.7.0 sessionwire/v1 -- 33 schemas, 33 fixtures -- and
removed Harness from the module graph. @looprig/protocol's TypeScript
schema mirror still describes the Harness-era wire contract, so it
disagrees with the newly mirrored Core contract. The Wave 2 checkpoint
permits that drift; reconciling it is Wave 4C protocol work and is blocked
on Factory contract fixtures that do not exist yet.
This is an allowance for a KNOWN, DATED, BOUNDED failure, not a way to stop
running the suite. It records three things, and the gate asserts all three:
suiteFiles -- every test file the suite is expected to RUN. The gate fails
if the set vitest reports differs in either direction. Without this floor
a file renamed out of vitest.config.ts's include glob simply stops
guarding and the gate still exits 0; `git mv test/surface.test.ts
test/surface.spec.ts` was verified to do exactly that.
files[*].failingTests + files[*].tests -- for the seven drifted files that
are fast and deterministic, the exact set of failing test names and the
number of tests collected. A NEW failure inside a drifted file is a name
not on the list and fails the gate. A file that stops COLLECTING its tests
is a count that dropped and fails the gate.
files[*].granularityReason -- for the three drifted files that drive real
HTTP servers under 85-90s timeouts, why they stay file-granular. Their
per-test outcomes are machine-dependent; recording them would trade a real
gate for a flaky one. Each says so for itself rather than sharing one
blanket justification, because the earlier blanket version was true of
these three and was applied to all ten.
An entry must have exactly one of failingTests or granularityReason. The
gate fails if a file listed here stops failing, so retiring an entry is a
deliberate edit in the same commit that fixes the drift.
STATED COST, so no reader has to infer it: inside the three HTTP files a new
failure is still indistinguishable from the drift. Everything else -- the 26
healthy files and the seven fast drifted ones -- gates.
